mechanism_narrative: A sustained low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS < 0.5%) compresses discount rates and stimulates equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 forward 20-day returns.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS < 0.5% in 60% of instances but 20-day forward returns are negative in > 50% of those instances.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) exceeds 5.5%, it signals a weak labor market and economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 forward 5-day returns.
failure_condition: UNRATE > 5.5% in 60% of instances but 5-day forward returns are positive in > 50% of those instances.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in housing starts (HOUST) and industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 0.5% in the prior month signals a broad economic slowdown, causing negative S&P 500 forward 60-day returns.
candidate_trigger: HOUST decline > 0.5% and INDPRO decline > 0.5% in the prior month
failure_condition: In 60% of instances where HOUST and INDPRO both decline by >0.5%, 60-day forward returns are positive.

mechanism_narrative: In high inflation regimes (CPIAUCSL > 2.5%), a rise in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) compresses equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward 20-day returns.
failure_condition: In periods with CPIAUCSL > 2.5%, FEDFUNDS rises by at least 0.1% but 20-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) signals a strong labor market and economic expansion, producing positive S&P 500 forward 5-day returns.
failure_condition: PAYEMS rise > 0.5% in the prior month but 5-day forward returns are negative in > 50% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) exceed 1200 thousand units, it signals strong consumer demand and economic growth, leading to positive S&P 500 forward 60-day returns.
failure_condition: HOUST > 1200 in 60% of instances but 60-day forward returns are negative in > 50% of those instances.

mechanism_narrative: In low interest rate environments (FEDFUNDS < 0.5%), rising consumer credit (RSAFS) stimulates economic activity and equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 forward 20-day returns.
failure_condition: RSAFS rises > 0.5% and FEDFUNDS < 0.5% but 20-day forward returns are negative in > 50% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: In supply shock regimes (INDPRO decline > 1% in the prior month), reduced industrial output leads to negative S&P 500 forward 5-day returns due to lower corporate profits.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO decline > 1% in the prior month
failure_condition: INDPRO decline > 1% in the prior month but 5-day forward returns are positive in > 50% of instances.
